title: a proof run outside the tester's seal leaves no fixture emission in the live logs tree
intention: A proof run bare (python3 <proof>, a script file, any spelling proofgate cannot see) leaves no projector.append_entry emission for a fixture world in the live ~/.cairn/logs; the seal Q#101's answer picks closes that spelling, and a sealed run's emissions still land in the swap.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on akiendelllinux by akiendelllinux_cc_0: ~/.cairn/logs/charter/0 holds 7,435 append_entry emissions, 4,910 with values.location under /tmp/ (hand_crossing_fixture_*, every_class_fixme_fixture*, t2-ticket-*, cairn-artifact-door-proof-*), dated 2026-09-05..11-13, peaking 2,258 on 09-08. A sealed bin/cairn test of test_artifact_door.py and test_a_ticket_queues_itself_at_a_gate.py wrote 0 new files there. So the source is unsealed runs, Q#101's spelling.
traces_to: Law 7 (a record of truth is never fed a manufactured error); CP6. The instance seal exists so a proof cannot dirty instance-space (tester/isolation.py:261-288, :511).
how: After Q#101 is answered, the seal it names covers the bare spelling; a red-first proof drives a bare run of a one-append fixture under a scratch stamp and reads the live logs tree before and after.

clauses.claim: a proof that calls projector.append_entry on a /tmp fixture history, run bare the way Q#101's answer names, leaves no new file under the live ~/.cairn/logs (find -newer before/after)
the same proof under bin/cairn test still passes, and its emission lands in the swap, not live (no regression of the instance seal)

decisions.text: D1: the seal Q#101's answer names covers the bare spelling. For (a) the site is cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py; for (b) it is bin/cmd/proofgate and the ticket re-bounds at READY.
D2: one red-first proof, one tooth per clause, driving a bare run of a one-append fixture.

out: projector.append_entry (emitting is right; the location is wrong)
log sweep and cleanup of the leaked files
